title: Lit Windows
statement: A building's lights are stored as one whole number `n`: in its binary form, each 1 is a lit window and each 0 a dark one. Return how many windows are lit, that is, how many 1 bits `n` has.

answerKey.pattern: Clear the lowest 1 bit with n & (n - 1) until n is 0
keyPoints: n - 1 flips the lowest 1 bit and every 0 below it
n & (n - 1) therefore removes exactly the lowest 1 bit
Count how many times this can be done before n becomes 0
Alternative: check n & 1 and shift right, 31 times
answerKey.timeComplexity: O(number of 1 bits), at most 31 steps
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Convert to a binary string and count '1' characters: O(31) with extra memory

hints: How can you look at the last bit of a number?
n & 1 is the last bit, and n >>> 1 drops it. Or think about what n & (n - 1) does.
Count the 1 bits by removing the lowest one each time with n = n & (n - 1).
